title: Most Career Test Runs
blurb: Career Test runs for the leading batters since the first Test at Melbourne in 1877. The record passes from Shrewsbury to Clem Hill, Hobbs, Hammond and a run of post-war greats before Gavaskar breaks 10,000; Tendulkar then sets the 15,921 mark, and Joe Root is now the only active batter chasing it.

source.name: ESPNcricinfo Statsguru
source.note: Statsguru career totals at year ends (every 4 years 1880–2024, plus 1877, 1879, 1929, 1970, 1982–83, 1993–94, 2005–07, 2025), Sep/Oct 2008 and Oct 2026. Includes the 2005 ICC World XI Test; batters outside the top 100 on a sample date show as 0.

milestones.title: Hobbs passes Clem Hill
milestones.text: Jack Hobbs overtakes Clem Hill's 3,412, the record since the early 1900s, and retires in 1930 with 5,410.

milestones.title: Hammond takes the record
milestones.text: Wally Hammond passes Hobbs in 1937 and finishes on 7,249, a record that stands for more than 30 years.

milestones.title: Bradman's final duck
milestones.text: Needing 4 runs for 7,000 and a Test average of 100, Don Bradman is bowled second ball at The Oval. He ends on 6,996.

milestones.title: Gavaskar passes Boycott
milestones.text: Sunil Gavaskar overtakes Geoffrey Boycott's 8,114 against West Indies at Ahmedabad to become Test cricket's top scorer.

milestones.title: First to 10,000
milestones.text: Gavaskar becomes the first batter to reach 10,000 Test runs, against Pakistan at Ahmedabad, and retires on 10,122.

milestones.title: Border overtakes Gavaskar
milestones.text: Allan Border passes Gavaskar at Christchurch in 1993 and retires the next year with 11,174 runs.

milestones.title: Tendulkar passes Lara
milestones.text: At Mohali, Sachin Tendulkar passes Brian Lara's 11,953. He retires in 2013 with 15,921, still the record.

milestones.title: Root passes Ponting for No. 2
milestones.text: Joe Root's 2025 hundred at Old Trafford takes him past Ricky Ponting's 13,378. By Oct 2026 he has 14,278.
